concept.title: VARIANT Data Type ( or higher only)

conbody.p: VARIANT data typeA semi-structured type that holds values such as JSON documents. The values are stored in the Parquet Variant binary encoding, which Iceberg uses for the VARIANT type of format version 3 tables. Starting in , Impala can read the VARIANT columns of Iceberg tables that other engines, such as Spark or Trino, wrote.
The column type appears as VARIANT in the output of DESCRIBE and SHOW CREATE TABLE. VARIANT is not a reserved word.

section.title: Reading VARIANT columns
section.p: Impala reads only top-level, unshredded VARIANT columns, in Iceberg tables whose data files are in Parquet format.

section.title: How VARIANT values are returned
section.p: Impala returns a VARIANT value as its JSON text. Clients receive the column as STRING. Over JDBC, the DATA_TYPE of the column is VARCHAR and the TYPE_NAME is VARIANT. The JSON text follows these rules:

ul.li: A SQL NULL value is returned as NULL. A variant null is a regular value, and it is returned as the text null.
Booleans and numbers, including decimals and floating-point numbers, are returned without quotes, for example true, 42 and 14.3.
Strings are returned in double quotes, with the JSON escape sequences.
Objects and arrays are returned as JSON objects and arrays.
Binary values are returned as base64 strings in double quotes, for example "CgsMDQ==".
Dates, and timestamps without time zone, are returned as strings in double quotes, for example "2024-11-07" and "2024-11-07 12:33:54.123456000".
Times, timestamps with time zone and UUIDs are returned as the string "<unsupported-type>".

section.p: To tell a SQL NULL from a variant null, use the IS NULL operator. v IS NULL is true only for a SQL NULL, and it is false for a variant null. In contrast, variant_get(v, '$') IS NULL is true for a variant null, because variant_get() returns a SQL NULL for it.

section.title: Functions for VARIANT values
section.p: Starting in , Impala has the following built-in functions for VARIANT values:

ul.li: variant_get(VARIANT v, STRING path) returns the VARIANT value at the path. You can chain the calls, for example variant_get(variant_get(v, '$.a'), '$.b').
variant_get(VARIANT v, STRING path, STRING type) returns the value at the path as a SQL value of the given type.
try_variant_get() has the same two forms as variant_get(). It returns NULL instead of failing the query when a value cannot be converted.
variant_to_json(VARIANT v) returns the JSON text of the value as a STRING.

section.p: The path starts with $, followed by any number of .field and [index] steps. For example, $ is the whole value, $.user.name is a field of an object, and $.items[0].id is a field of the first element of an array. Field names are case-sensitive. A field name cannot be empty or contain . or [, and there is no syntax to quote such a name. An index is a non-negative integer. Impala checks the syntax of a constant path during analysis. The first argument must be a VARIANT.
variant_get() and try_variant_get() return NULL if the input is NULL, if the path does not exist, or if the value at the path is a variant null. variant_to_json() returns NULL if the input is NULL.

The third argument of the typed form must be a string literal, one of boolean, tinyint, smallint, int, bigint, float, double, string and date. The names are not case-sensitive. Other types, such as decimal and timestamp, are not supported. The function converts the value at the path as follows:

ul.li: boolean: a variant boolean, or a string that Impala can parse as a boolean.

tinyint, smallint, int, bigint: an integer of any width, or a string that Impala can parse as an integer. The value must fit in the requested type. Impala does not convert floating-point values to integers.
float, double: a floating-point value, an integer, or a string that Impala can parse as a number. The value must be in the range of float for the float type.
date: a variant date, or a string in the YYYY-MM-DD format. Impala does not convert integers to dates.

string: a string is returned without the quotes. Other values are returned as their JSON text, and dates, timestamps and binary values are returned without the quotes of the JSON string. Times, timestamps with time zone and UUIDs cannot be converted.

section.p: If a value cannot be converted, or it does not fit in the requested type, variant_get() raises an error and try_variant_get() returns NULL. If the function finds that the VARIANT value is corrupt, variant_get() raises an error and try_variant_get() returns NULL with a warning. variant_to_json() returns NULL with a warning if it cannot render the value.

section.title: Limitations
section.p: Shredded VARIANT values in Parquet files, and VARIANT columns in Avro or ORC data files, are not supported.
A VARIANT that is nested in an ARRAY, MAP or STRUCT column cannot be queried. DESCRIBE still works, and you can query the other columns of the table.

The type is read-only. You cannot declare VARIANT columns with Impala, so you cannot use the type in the column definitions of the CREATE TABLE and ALTER TABLE statements, or as the target type of CAST. You cannot cast a VARIANT to another type either. To get the JSON text of a value as a STRING, use variant_to_json().

You cannot insert data into a table that has a VARIANT column. The INSERT, UPDATE, MERGE and OPTIMIZE TABLE statements fail on such a table, and the CREATE TABLE AS SELECT and INSERT ... SELECT statements cannot return a VARIANT.
VARIANT values cannot be compared, sorted or hashed. You cannot use a VARIANT expression in the following clauses:

ul.li: ORDER BY, GROUP BY and SELECT DISTINCT.
UNION (without ALL), INTERSECT and EXCEPT.
CASE and DECODE expressions that return a VARIANT.
PARTITION BY and ORDER BY in analytic functions.

section.p: With the type argument, variant_get() and try_variant_get() return a primitive type, so you can use them in these clauses, for example GROUP BY variant_get(v, '$.country', 'string').

Apart from IS [NOT] NULL and the functions above, the built-in operators and functions, including the aggregate functions, do not accept VARIANT arguments. For example, v = v, count(v) and coalesce(v, v) are not supported.
You can return VARIANT values through UNION ALL, joins, inline views, views and WITH clauses.

section.title: Limits and errors in the values
section.p: Impala converts a VARIANT value to its JSON text for the query result, for variant_to_json(), and for the string type of variant_get(). The conversion fails if:

ul.li: A value is nested more than 100 levels deep.
A DATE in the value is outside the range 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31, or a TIMESTAMP is outside the range 1400-01-01 to 9999-12-31. Other engines can write such values.
The value has a corrupt encoding.
COMPUTE STATS does not compute statistics for VARIANT columns.
SHOW CREATE TABLE prints the column as v VARIANT. You cannot run the output of the statement, because you cannot declare VARIANT columns with Impala.

The Hive metastore has no VARIANT type. When Impala writes the schema of the table to the metastore, it stores a VARIANT column as struct<metadata:binary,value:binary>. Take this into account when other engines or tools read the schema of the table from the metastore.
